s1.syndrome_frame: Chronic oral erosions with systemic symptoms and a mediastinal mass
salient_findings: Lingual biopsy showing epidermal acanthosis and band-like lymphohistiocytic infiltrate
key_facts: Patient is a White man in his 50s
Oral erosions began 2 years before presentation
Patient has a history of recurrent respiratory infections and diarrhea
Previous intestinal biopsy showed unspecific findings and absence of apoptosis
Patient reported a 5-kg weight loss due to impaired intake
Mediastinal mass was detected during chest radiography for pneumonia
Physical examination revealed whitish edematous lacy patches with erosions on the tongue and buccal mucosa
Skin and nails were not involved
Lingual biopsy showed epidermal acanthosis with scattered necrotic keratinocytes and basal-layer vacuolation
Direct immunofluorescence showed fibrinogen deposition along basement membrane
Decreased IgG serum level
Decreased total B lymphocyte count
Increased CD8+ T count with inverted CD4:CD8 ratio
Positron emission tomography revealed a 10-cm hypercapturing extrapulmonary mass
Surgical excision and histopathology of mediastinal mass showed type AB thymoma, Masaoka-Koga stage 2A

shortlist.label: Thymoma
shortlist.why_kept: Mediastinal mass detected and histopathology confirmed type AB thymoma

shortlist.label: Paraneoplastic pemphigus
shortlist.why_kept: Chronic oral erosions and thymoma, a known association with paraneoplastic pemphigus

shortlist.label: Good's syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Thymoma and decreased IgG serum level, consistent with Good's syndrome

shortlist.label: Mucous membrane pemphigoid
shortlist.why_kept: Oral erosions and fibrinogen deposition along basement membrane, consistent with mucous membrane pemphigoid

shortlist.label: Autoimmune lymphoproliferative syndrome
shortlist.why_kept: Recurrent infections, decreased IgG, and inverted CD4:CD8 ratio, suggesting an underlying immunodeficiency
